reader.answers:
1. Reuben_404 is afraid of being rejected or seen flinching when someone sees their short, wide, hard-left shaft and mismatched nuts, or their messy life.
2. They constantly narrate their own panic and defense mechanisms in real time, offering preemptive "full disclosures" and exit clauses so the other person leaves before Reuben_404 gets hurt.
3. They grew up cropped out of the edge of family photos because of how they were built.
4. They dropped it at the end, plainly explaining the mirror test without self-auditing and promising, "I am not going anywhere."
5. Brick_haus is afraid of being seen as "too much" and having people step back so they don't get bruised when she leans her towering, heavy weight on them.
6. She hides behind numbered lists, rigorous standards, scheduling buffers, and talk of doorway geometry to pretend she is detached and in control.
7. She grew up so oversized in a cramped terrace house that she cracked the doorframe at fourteen.
8. She dropped it in the final turn, explicitly saying "no numbers" and asking Reuben_404 to stay and let her bruise them against the booth.
9. When Reuben_404 hid behind meta-narration in Turn 7 instead of matching her bath-towel confession, Brick_haus retreated back into her "high-value" scheduling buffers and threatened to take Tuesday off the calendar until Reuben_404 finally gave her real honesty.
10. "Standing up, a short wide shaft with a hard-left hook and a left nut the size of a plum looks less like a silhouette and more like a lowercase b." It is an unforgettable, deadpan visual that captures both the absurdity of the world and Reuben_404's self-consciousness.
11. I laughed in Turn 4 when both of their intense pieces of body-modification hardware—a $189 titanium posture clip and a 240-pound equestrian harness—turned out to be holding a bag of coffee shut and propping a hallway door open.
